messages:
jas: starting thread: proposal to shift attribute-enrichment (customer/billing tags) downstream to ingest while keeping a slim envelope at the edge. main wins: single canonicalizer, simpler join logic, less edge churn. main risks: extra ingest IO and eventual consistency for billing. thoughts?
marta: we need to define the join surface for post-enrich. join on trace_hash + envelope_id? what about late attributions from downstream services that only surface hours later?
leo: propose a 3-phase flow:
1) edge emits slim envelope: {env_id, trace_hash, route, minimal_keys, client_sig}
2) ingest persists envelope, runs policy + canonicalizer, decides keep/drop and writes tombstone if dropped
3) async enrichment worker pulls retained envelopes, attaches heavyweight customer attrs (from canonical map + lookups) and emits final billing rows
claire: clarifying q: async enrich => billing becomes eventually consistent. how do we surface that to customers & analytics?
emil: two modes: provisional (fast, used in near-real-time dashboards) and authoritative (post-enrichment). UI can show a "pending enrichment" state. enterprise/dedicated tenants can opt into authoritative-only mode.
jas: storage plan: keep slim envelope + tombstone in a TTL'd table. default retention = 2h. enrichment queue reads retained envelopes; if enrichment misses the TTL, attribution is dropped (or routed to a late-backfill path for paid customers).
marta: per-tenant requirements: Dedicated/private customers may require no tombstoning. add tenant flag in envelope: keep_fidelity=true. also add an alert when enrich-lag > 10m for prod tenants.
leo: canonicalizer rules: deterministic normalizer for billing_key and service names (lowercase, whitespace collapse, strip known prefixes). maintain a canonical map in KV with versioned snapshots. ingest stamps canonical_version on each envelope for auditability.
claire: ops ask: what's the cost hit? rough numbers pls.
emil: back-of-envelope: ingest CPU up ~5% for canonicalization at peak RPS; enrichment workers ~0.3 vCPU per 10k envelopes/s processing (including KV lookups). tombstone table retention 2h -> ~2M rows/hr/region (depends on traffic). will refine with real traffic profile.
jas: retry/dedupe: include client_attempt_id and a logical_event_id in envelope to dedupe at ingest and avoid double-counting. enrichment consumer must be idempotent.
marta: security: canonical map updates require tight RBAC + audit trail. also sign envelopes at edge (client_sig) to prevent spoofing of keep_fidelity flags.
claire: UX: add GET /ingest/enrich-status?env_id=... for debug and support. also expose metrics: ingest.enrich.queue.depth, enrich.lag.p50/p95, enrich.failure_rate.
ingest-bot: ticket created: INF-5982 "post-sample enrichment design" -> tasks: schema bump (slim-envelope), tombstone TTL config, enrich-worker autoscaling, canonicalizer KV snapshotting, auth for canonical updates.
leo: next steps: run 48h dry-run where enrichment runs in passive/observe mode (no writes to billing). capture provisional_vs_authoritative mismatch metric and enrichment.lag histograms. jas to own the dry-run infra. marta to spec tenant override API. emil to prototype idempotent enrich consumer. claire to size alerts and dashboard changes.
jas: decision summary: move heavy attribute resolution async to enrichment pipeline, keep slim envelope at edge, default tombstone TTL 2h with per-tenant override for full fidelity. run dry-run before any rollout. proceeding with infra tickets. :white_check_mark:
